NSAIDs/aspirin, alcohol, and opioids commonly exacerbate urticaria even when not the primary cause; advise avoidance or substitution when possible. Also minimize any patient-specific physical triggers (pressure, cold, heat, exercise, etc.), though this presentation is not linked to hot showers.

Refer (dermatology/allergy or for biopsy) if individual lesions last >24 h, are painful/burning more than pruritic, leave purpura, bruising, or hyperpigmentation, or if systemic features appear (fever, arthralgias, abdominal pain, angioedema with airway risk, or other concerning signs). Standard fleeting pruritic wheals do not require this work-up.

### Escalation if not controlled
If symptoms persist despite maximally up-dosed second-generation antihistamine:
- Refer to allergy/dermatology.
- Preferred next step is omalizumab (anti-IgE).
- For omalizumab-refractory disease, cyclosporine is the usual subsequent option (with monitoring).

- Evaluate and treat comorbid contributors when present (e.g., thyroid autoimmunity association) but do not delay symptomatic control.
